overview.eyebrow: AN ACADEMIC EXPLORATION IN COMMERCE INTELLIGENCE
overview.summaryLine2: A proposed decision support system for more informed e-commerce operations.
overview.bottomCaption: FROM OPERATIONAL DATA TO INFORMED DECISIONS

challenges: Changing sales patterns make it difficult to anticipate how much stock will be needed.
Stockouts miss opportunities. Excess inventory ties up resources and increases holding costs.
Disconnected records make a consistent view of business performance difficult to maintain.
Revenue alone does not explain the contribution of each product after relevant costs.
problem.label: THE PROBLEM
problem.intro: For small and medium-sized sellers, more data does not always mean a clearer next step.
problem.description: Sales, stock levels and costs often live in separate files. Understanding what to order, when to replenish and which products create value requires connecting those signals.

system.label: THE PROPOSED SYSTEM
system.description: CommerceAIQ aims to connect predictive analysis with practical inventory and profitability decisions in a single, understandable workflow.
system.note: Human judgment remains central to every operational decision.

research.label: RESEARCH OBJECTIVES
research.description: We are investigating how predictive methods can support everyday commerce decisions, with clear baselines and measurable evaluation.

capabilities.label: SYSTEM CAPABILITIES
capabilities.visualNote: Visual signals are schematic illustrations, not measured performance.

methods: Identify seller workflows, functional needs, data limitations and project constraints.
Define system boundaries, modules, data structures and an understandable analytical interface.
Compare forecasting methods using chronological splits and suitable error metrics; examine replenishment and margin assumptions.
Plan data validation, software tests and usability evaluation. Document uncertainty and limitations.
approach.label: ENGINEERING APPROACH
approach.intro: The intended contribution is the connection: forecasting demand, planning inventory and considering profitability together.
approach.description: We will investigate a practical integration of these methods rather than assume that a more complex model produces a better decision.
approach.disciplineDescription: Software engineering meets industrial engineering through inventory planning, replenishment policies and operations optimization.
approach.ethicsDescription: Data privacy, explainable recommendations and honest evaluation will guide the proposed system. Forecasts support decisions; they do not guarantee outcomes.

documents.label: PROJECT DOCUMENTATION
documents.description: An evolving archive of research and engineering deliverables. Reports will be available here as they are published.
documents.publicationNote: Only published, available files are linked. No draft or placeholder reports are presented as final submissions.
